compatibilityIssues: Migration from Web Forms to .NET 8 required
upgradeSteps: Refactor Web Forms to Razor Pages/MVC

issues.impact: All data access code must be rewritten. DbContext inheritance, entity configurations, LINQ queries, and database initialization logic all require migration. Estimated effort: 40-60 hours.
issues.description: The application uses Entity Framework 6.2.0 which is NOT compatible with .NET 8. This is a .NET Framework-only package that must be replaced with Entity Framework Core 8.0.0.
issues.recommendation: Replace EntityFramework 6.2.0 with Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore 8.0.0, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer 8.0.0, and Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design 8.0.0. All DbContext classes must be migrated from System.Data.Entity.DbContext to Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.DbContext. Entity configurations must be updated from EntityTypeConfiguration to IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>.
issues.title: Entity Framework 6.2.0 Not Compatible with .NET 8

issues.impact: All logging statements across 11 files must be updated. LogManager.GetLogger calls must be replaced with dependency-injected ILogger<T>. Estimated effort: 12-16 hours.
issues.description: The application uses log4net 2.0.10 which is a legacy logging framework not recommended for .NET 8 applications.
issues.recommendation: Replace log4net with Microsoft.Extensions.Logging 8.0.0 or Serilog.AspNetCore 8.0.0. Update all ILog references to ILogger<T>. Configure logging in Program.cs. Remove log4Net.xml configuration and use appsettings.json for logging configuration.
issues.title: log4net 2.0.10 Not Recommended for .NET 8

issues.codeSnippet: Default.aspx, About.aspx, Contact.aspx, Catalog/Create.aspx, Catalog/Edit.aspx, Catalog/Details.aspx, Catalog/Delete.aspx
issues.impact: Complete UI layer rewrite required. All 7 pages plus their code-behind files must be migrated. Page lifecycle events (Page_Load, etc.) must be converted to PageModel handlers (OnGet, OnPost). Estimated effort: 50-70 hours.
issues.description: Application contains 7 .aspx Web Forms pages that must be migrated to Razor Pages or MVC. Web Forms is not supported in .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Migrate all .aspx pages to Razor Pages (.cshtml) with PageModel code-behind classes. Extract business logic from code-behind into service layer. Replace server controls with HTML and Tag Helpers. Implement proper Model-View-ViewModel pattern.
issues.title: ASP.NET Web Forms Pages Must Be Migrated to Razor Pages

issues.impact: User control functionality must be reimplemented as View Component. Estimated effort: 2-4 hours.
issues.description: Application contains 1 .ascx user control (ViewSwitcher.ascx) that must be migrated to View Components or Partial Views.
issues.recommendation: Convert ViewSwitcher.ascx to a ViewComponent in .NET 8. Create ViewSwitcherViewComponent class with InvokeAsync method. Create corresponding Razor view in Views/Shared/Components/ViewSwitcher/Default.cshtml.
issues.title: User Controls Must Be Migrated to View Components or Partial Views

issues.impact: Master page structure and all ContentPlaceHolder references must be updated. Estimated effort: 8-12 hours.
issues.description: Application uses Site.Master and Site.Mobile.Master which must be migrated to Layout Pages (_Layout.cshtml).
issues.recommendation: Convert Site.Master to _Layout.cshtml Razor Layout page. Replace ContentPlaceHolder controls with @RenderBody() and @RenderSection(). Remove runat="server" attributes. Convert ASP.NET server controls to standard HTML with Tag Helpers. Move master page code-behind logic to _ViewStart.cshtml or base PageModel class.
issues.title: Master Pages Not Supported in .NET 8

issues.impact: Complete application bootstrap redesign required. Autofac integration must be replaced or adapted. Estimated effort: 16-24 hours.
issues.description: Global.asax application startup logic must be migrated to Program.cs in .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Create Program.cs with minimal hosting model. Move application startup logic to builder.Services configuration. Replace Autofac container configuration with built-in DI container. Move database initialization to DbContext OnModelCreating or separate migration. Replace Application_BeginRequest with middleware.
issues.title: Global.asax Not Supported - Must Migrate to Program.cs

issues.codeSnippet:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<configuration>
  <connectionStrings>
    <add name="CatalogDBContext" connectionString="Data Source=(localdb)\MSSQLLocalDB; Initial Catalog=Microsoft.eShopOnContainers.Services.CatalogDb; Integrated Security=True; MultipleActiveResultSets=True;" providerName="System.Data.SqlClient" />
  </connectionStrings>
issues.impact: All configuration access code must be updated. ConfigurationManager.AppSettings and ConfigurationManager.ConnectionStrings must be replaced with IConfiguration. Estimated effort: 6-10 hours.
issues.description: Web.config configuration system is not used in .NET 8. Must migrate to appsettings.json and Program.cs.
issues.recommendation: Create appsettings.json and appsettings.Development.json files. Migrate connectionStrings to ConnectionStrings section. Move appSettings to root or custom sections. Configure options pattern in Program.cs. Replace ConfigurationManager with IConfiguration injection.
issues.title: Web.config Must Be Migrated to appsettings.json

issues.codeSnippet: using System.Web; using System.Web.UI; using System.Web.Optimization; using System.Web.Routing;
issues.impact: Massive refactoring required across 19 files. Every Web Forms page class must be redesigned. Estimated effort: 30-40 hours.
issues.description: Found 51 occurrences of System.Web namespace usage across 19 files. System.Web is not available in .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Replace all System.Web references: System.Web.UI.Page → PageModel, System.Web.Optimization → ASP.NET Core bundling/minification, System.Web.Routing → ASP.NET Core routing, System.Web.HttpContext → Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.HttpContext.
issues.title: System.Web References Throughout Application

issues.impact: Session state management code must be redesigned. IHttpContextAccessor must be configured and injected. Estimated effort: 4-6 hours.
issues.description: Found HttpContext.Current usage in 2 files (Global.asax.cs and Site.Master.cs). This static accessor is not available in .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Replace HttpContext.Current with IHttpContextAccessor dependency injection. Inject IHttpContextAccessor into classes that need HttpContext access. Access via httpContextAccessor.HttpContext. For middleware, HttpContext is available as parameter.
issues.title: HttpContext.Current Usage Must Be Replaced

issues.impact: Session configuration required in Program.cs. All Session access code must be updated. Consider architectural change to stateless design. Estimated effort: 8-12 hours.
issues.description: Application uses Session state (HttpContext.Current.Session). Session state works differently in ASP.NET Core and requires configuration.
issues.recommendation: Configure session state in Program.cs: builder.Services.AddDistributedMemoryCache() and builder.Services.AddSession(). Use app.UseSession() middleware. Access session via HttpContext.Session. Consider using distributed cache (Redis) for production scenarios or moving to stateless design.
issues.title: Session State Implementation Differs in .NET 8

issues.impact: Complete DI container reconfiguration required. Property injection in Web Forms must be replaced with constructor injection in Razor Pages. Estimated effort: 12-16 hours.
issues.description: Application uses Autofac.Integration.Web 4.0.0 which is designed for ASP.NET Web Forms and not compatible with .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Replace Autofac.Integration.Web with Autofac.Extensions.DependencyInjection for .NET 8. Update to Autofac 8.0.0. Migrate container configuration from Global.asax to Program.cs. Use builder.Host.UseServiceProviderFactory(new AutofacServiceProviderFactory()) pattern. Alternatively, consider using built-in ASP.NET Core DI container.
issues.title: Autofac Web Integration Package Not Compatible

issues.impact: Project file complete rewrite. Package references must be updated to .NET 8 compatible versions. Build process may need adjustments. Estimated effort: 6-10 hours.
issues.description: Project uses old-style .csproj format (ToolsVersion="12.0", packages.config). Must convert to SDK-style project targeting net8.0.
issues.recommendation: Convert to SDK-style project: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">. Set <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>. Migrate packages.config to PackageReference format. Remove unnecessary elements (HintPath, EmbeddedResource includes, etc.). Enable nullable reference types and implicit usings.
issues.title: Old Project Format Must Be Converted to SDK-Style

issues.impact: DbContext class requires significant refactoring. OnModelCreating methods must be updated. Connection string configuration moves to Program.cs. Estimated effort: 10-15 hours.
issues.description: CatalogDBContext inherits from System.Data.Entity.DbContext which must be changed to Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.DbContext.
issues.recommendation: Change base class to Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.DbContext. Replace connection string constructor with DbContextOptions<T> parameter. Update entity configurations from EntityTypeConfiguration<T> to IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>. Implement separate configuration classes. Configure options in Program.cs using builder.Services.AddDbContext<CatalogDBContext>().
issues.title: Entity Framework DbContext Must Migrate to EF Core

issues.impact: All entity configurations must be refactored into separate classes. Fluent API differences must be addressed. Estimated effort: 6-10 hours.
issues.description: Entity configurations use EF6 EntityTypeConfiguration<T> which is not compatible with EF Core IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>.
issues.recommendation: Create separate configuration classes implementing IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>. Move each Configure method to its own class (CatalogTypeConfiguration, CatalogBrandConfiguration, CatalogItemConfiguration). Update fluent API calls for EF Core differences (HasRequired → HasOne, etc.). Apply configurations using modelBuilder.ApplyConfiguration(new EntityConfiguration()).
issues.title: Entity Configuration Methods Incompatible with EF Core

issues.impact: Database initialization logic must be completely rewritten. Seed data approach changes. Migration system adoption required. Estimated effort: 8-12 hours.
issues.description: Application uses Database.SetInitializer<T> which is not available in EF Core. Must migrate to EF Core migrations.
issues.recommendation: Remove Database.SetInitializer usage. Implement database initialization using EF Core migrations (dotnet ef migrations add Initial). For seed data, override DbContext.OnModelCreating and use modelBuilder.Entity<T>().HasData(). Alternatively, create a database initializer service that runs at application startup.
issues.title: Database Initialization Strategy Not Supported in EF Core

issues.impact: Every page's code-behind logic must be refactored to PageModel pattern. Data binding approach changes fundamentally. Estimated effort: 20-30 hours for 7 pages.
issues.description: All Page_Load events and Web Forms page lifecycle must be migrated to Razor Pages PageModel handlers.
issues.recommendation: Replace Page_Load with OnGet() or OnGetAsync() handlers in PageModel classes. Move data loading logic to handler methods. Use dependency injection for services instead of property injection. Replace Page.RouteData with route parameters in handler methods. Update data binding approach from DataBind() to Razor syntax.
issues.title: Page Lifecycle Events Must Be Replaced

issues.impact: All UI markup must be rewritten. Server control events must be replaced with form handlers. JavaScript requirements change. Estimated effort: 25-35 hours.
issues.description: ASP.NET server controls (ListView, HyperLink, ScriptManager, etc.) are not available in .NET 8 Razor Pages.
issues.recommendation: Replace ListView with standard HTML table and @foreach loop in Razor. Replace HyperLink controls with <a asp-page="" asp-route-id=""> Tag Helpers. Remove ScriptManager and use standard script tags. Replace UpdatePanel with AJAX calls using JavaScript. Replace validation controls with data annotations and asp-validation-* Tag Helpers.
issues.title: Server Controls Must Be Replaced with HTML and Tag Helpers

issues.impact: Routing system complete redesign. All route references in views must be updated. Estimated effort: 6-10 hours.
issues.description: Web Forms routing in RouteConfig.RegisterRoutes must be replaced with ASP.NET Core endpoint routing.
issues.recommendation: Remove RouteConfig class. Configure routing in Program.cs using app.MapRazorPages(). Use Razor Pages conventions for routing or add custom routes with [Route] attributes on PageModels. Replace RouteUrl helpers in views with asp-page and asp-route-* Tag Helpers.
issues.title: Routing Configuration Must Migrate to Endpoint Routing

issues.impact: Bundling configuration must be rewritten. Bundle references in views must be updated. Consider modern frontend build tools. Estimated effort: 8-12 hours.
issues.description: System.Web.Optimization bundling is not available in .NET 8. Must migrate to modern bundling approach.
issues.recommendation: Remove System.Web.Optimization. Use WebOptimizer NuGet package for bundling/minification in .NET 8, or use build-time bundling with tools like webpack, Vite, or esbuild. Configure in Program.cs: builder.Services.AddWebOptimizer(). Reference individual files in development, bundled files in production using environment Tag Helper.
issues.title: Bundling and Minification System Must Be Replaced

issues.impact: Multiple features need reimplementation using ASP.NET Core equivalents. Estimated effort: 10-15 hours.
issues.description: Multiple Microsoft.AspNet.* packages are .NET Framework-only and not compatible with .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Remove all Microsoft.AspNet.* packages. FriendlyUrls: Use ASP.NET Core routing conventions. ScriptManager: Remove, use standard script tags. SessionState: Use ASP.NET Core session middleware. Web.Optimization: Use WebOptimizer or build tools. No direct replacements needed as functionality is built into ASP.NET Core.
issues.title: Microsoft.AspNet Packages Not Compatible with .NET 8

issues.impact: Logging code in 11+ files must be updated. All logger instances must use dependency injection. Estimated effort: 8-12 hours.
issues.description: log4net's LogManager.GetLogger pattern used throughout application must be replaced with ILogger<T> dependency injection.
issues.recommendation: Replace all LogManager.GetLogger calls with ILogger<T> constructor injection. Update logging calls: _log.Info() → _logger.LogInformation(), _log.Debug() → _logger.LogDebug(), _log.Error() → _logger.LogError(). Configure logging in Program.cs using builder.Logging or Serilog. Remove log4Net.xml file.
issues.title: LogManager.GetLogger Pattern Must Be Replaced

issues.impact: All PageModel classes must add constructors and refactor to constructor injection pattern. Service registration changes. Estimated effort: 6-10 hours.
issues.description: Application uses Autofac property injection (public ICatalogService CatalogService { get; set; }) which is not the standard pattern in ASP.NET Core.
issues.recommendation: Replace property injection with constructor injection in all PageModel classes. Add constructor parameters for all dependencies: public IndexModel(ICatalogService catalogService, ILogger<IndexModel> logger). Store dependencies in readonly fields. Configure services in Program.cs using builder.Services.AddScoped<ICatalogService, CatalogService>().
issues.title: Property Injection Pattern Not Supported in Razor Pages

issues.impact: All data binding code must be removed and replaced with Razor syntax. View markup changes significantly. Estimated effort: 8-12 hours.
issues.description: Web Forms data binding (DataSource, DataBind()) must be replaced with Razor syntax in .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Remove DataSource and DataBind() calls. Set Model property in PageModel OnGet handler. Use Razor syntax in .cshtml to iterate: @foreach(var item in Model.Data) { <tr>... }. Use strongly-typed PageModel properties accessed via Model in views.
issues.title: Data Binding Approach Fundamentally Different

issues.impact: Validation approach changes but security is enhanced by default in ASP.NET Core. Review all input handling. Estimated effort: 2-4 hours.
issues.description: Web.config contains requestValidationMode="2.0" which is obsolete and not applicable in .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Remove requestValidationMode setting. ASP.NET Core has automatic request validation and XSS protection built-in. Ensure proper input validation using data annotations, FluentValidation, or custom validation attributes. Enable CORS policy if needed. Use [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] on form POST handlers.
issues.title: Request Validation Mode Configuration Obsolete

issues.codeSnippet:
<httpModules>
  <add name="ContainerDisposal" type="Autofac.Integration.Web.ContainerDisposalModule, Autofac.Integration.Web" />
  <add name="PropertyInjection" type="Autofac.Integration.Web.Forms.PropertyInjectionModule, Autofac.Integration.Web" />
  <add name="TelemetryCorrelationHttpModule" type="Microsoft.AspNet.TelemetryCorrelation.TelemetryCorrelationHttpModule" />
  <add name="ApplicationInsightsWebTracking" type="Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.Web.ApplicationInsightsHttpModule" />
</httpModules>
issues.impact: HTTP module functionality must be replaced with middleware or built-in features. Application Insights integration changes. Estimated effort: 8-12 hours.
issues.description: Web.config defines HTTP modules (ContainerDisposal, PropertyInjection, TelemetryCorrelation, ApplicationInsights) which must be replaced with ASP.NET Core middleware.
issues.recommendation: Replace HTTP modules with middleware in Program.cs pipeline. ContainerDisposal: handled by built-in DI scope management. PropertyInjection: not needed with constructor injection. TelemetryCorrelation: use app.UseW3CLogging() or Application Insights SDK. ApplicationInsights: use builder.Services.AddApplicationInsightsTelemetry().
issues.title: HTTP Modules Must Be Replaced with Middleware

issues.impact: Entity configuration syntax changes but functionality remains same. All relationship configurations need updating. Estimated effort: 2-4 hours.
issues.description: EF6 relationship configuration (HasRequired, WithMany) has different syntax in EF Core (HasOne, WithMany).
issues.recommendation: Update relationship configurations for EF Core syntax: HasRequired → HasOne, IsRequired → IsRequired(). Example: builder.HasOne(ci => ci.CatalogBrand).WithMany().HasForeignKey(ci => ci.CatalogBrandId).IsRequired(). Review all relationships and update accordingly.
issues.title: Entity Framework Relationship Configuration Syntax Changes

issues.impact: DbContext constructor must change. Connection string configuration moves to Program.cs. Estimated effort: 2-3 hours.
issues.description: EF6 constructor pattern with connection string name not supported in EF Core.
issues.recommendation: Replace with DbContextOptions pattern: public CatalogDBContext(DbContextOptions<CatalogDBContext> options) : base(options). Configure connection string in Program.cs: builder.Services.AddDbContext<CatalogDBContext>(options => options.UseSqlServer(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("CatalogDBContext"))).
issues.title: EF6 Database Context Constructor Pattern Obsolete

issues.codeSnippet:
var itemsOnPage = db.CatalogItems
    .Include(c => c.CatalogBrand)
    .Include(c => c.CatalogType)
    .OrderBy(c => c.Id)
    .Skip(pageSize * pageIndex)
    .Take(pageSize)
    .ToList();
issues.impact: Include statements should work but need testing. May need to enable change tracking or configure loading strategy. Estimated effort: 2-4 hours for testing and validation.
issues.description: EF Core handles Include() and lazy loading differently than EF6. Explicit loading strategy needed.
issues.recommendation: Review all Include() usage. EF Core does not support lazy loading by default. Either: 1) Use explicit Include() for all navigations (current code should work), 2) Enable lazy loading proxies with Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Proxies package, or 3) Use explicit loading with Load() method. Prefer explicit Include() for better performance.
issues.title: Include() Method Behavior May Differ in EF Core

issues.impact: Disposal is automatic with proper DI registration. Verify service lifetimes are configured correctly. Estimated effort: 1-2 hours.
issues.description: Manual service disposal (IDisposable implementation) handled differently in ASP.NET Core DI container.
issues.recommendation: ASP.NET Core DI container handles disposal automatically for scoped/transient services. Keep IDisposable implementation but rely on DI container for disposal. Register as scoped: builder.Services.AddScoped<ICatalogService, CatalogService>(). DbContext disposal handled automatically. Consider removing manual disposal if service registered properly.
issues.title: Service Disposal Pattern Changes in ASP.NET Core

issues.impact: Telemetry configuration approach changes. Application Insights SDK must be updated. Estimated effort: 2-4 hours.
issues.description: ApplicationInsights.config XML configuration must be replaced with Program.cs configuration.
issues.recommendation: Remove ApplicationInsights.config file. Configure Application Insights in Program.cs: builder.Services.AddApplicationInsightsTelemetry(builder.Configuration["ApplicationInsights:InstrumentationKey"]). Add instrumentation key to appsettings.json. Update to latest Application Insights SDK for ASP.NET Core.
issues.title: Application Insights Configuration Must Migrate

issues.impact: Form handling pattern changes. All form POST handlers must be refactored. Validation attributes may need updates. Estimated effort: 6-10 hours.
issues.description: ModelState.IsValid usage pattern differs slightly in Razor Pages PageModel.
issues.recommendation: In Razor Pages, ModelState.IsValid is checked in OnPost handler. Return Page() if invalid to redisplay form with errors. Use [BindProperty] attribute on PageModel properties. Replace Response.Redirect with return RedirectToPage(). Use data annotations on view models for validation. Example: public async Task<IActionResult> OnPostAsync() { if (!ModelState.IsValid) return Page(); ... return RedirectToPage("./Index"); }
issues.title: ModelState Validation Works Differently in Razor Pages

issues.impact: All redirect statements must be updated. Handler methods need return type changes. Estimated effort: 2-4 hours.
issues.description: Response.Redirect pattern must be replaced with IActionResult returns in Razor Pages.
issues.recommendation: Replace Response.Redirect with return RedirectToPage(). Use RedirectToPage("./Index") for same folder, RedirectToPage("/Index") for root. Use RedirectToPage with route values: RedirectToPage("./Edit", new { id = item.Id }). Handler method must return IActionResult or Task<IActionResult>.
issues.title: Response.Redirect Must Be Replaced with RedirectToPage

issues.impact: Session state needs explicit setup. Session access pattern remains similar but configuration required. Estimated effort: 2-3 hours.
issues.description: Session state must be explicitly configured in ASP.NET Core, not just declared in Web.config.
issues.recommendation: Add session configuration in Program.cs: builder.Services.AddDistributedMemoryCache(); builder.Services.AddSession(options => { options.IdleTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30); options.Cookie.HttpOnly = true; options.Cookie.IsEssential = true; }); Add app.UseSession() in middleware pipeline before app.MapRazorPages(). For production, consider distributed cache with Redis.
issues.title: Session State Configuration Required in Program.cs

issues.impact: All ListView controls must be converted to Razor loops. Significant markup changes. Estimated effort: 8-12 hours for all pages.
issues.description: Web Forms ListView ItemType strongly-typed binding not available in Razor Pages.
issues.recommendation:
Replace ListView with @foreach loop in Razor: @foreach(var item in Model.Data) { @item.Name... }. ListView templates become standard HTML. ItemTemplate becomes loop body. EmptyDataTemplate becomes @if(!Model.Data.Any()) {

No items

}. Strongly-typed access via @item.
issues.title: ItemType Binding in ListView Must Be Replaced

issues.impact: All route URL generation must be updated. Named routes need redesign. All navigation links need Tag Helper conversion. Estimated effort: 4-6 hours.
issues.description: Web Forms GetRouteUrl helper must be replaced with Tag Helper attributes in Razor Pages.
issues.recommendation: Replace with asp-page Tag Helper: Edit. Remove named routes and use page-based routing. Update route configuration to use Razor Pages conventions. Use asp-route-{paramName} for route parameters.
issues.title: GetRouteUrl Helper Not Available in Razor Pages

issues.impact: All configuration access must use DI. Settings classes may be needed. Configuration structure may need reorganization. Estimated effort: 4-6 hours.
issues.description: ConfigurationManager.AppSettings static access must be replaced with IConfiguration injection.
issues.recommendation: Replace ConfigurationManager with IConfiguration dependency injection. In Program.cs or services, inject IConfiguration: builder.Services.AddSingleton<MyService>(sp => new MyService(builder.Configuration.GetValue<bool>("UseMockData"))). Use Options pattern: create settings class, configure with builder.Services.Configure<AppSettings>(builder.Configuration), inject IOptions<AppSettings>.
issues.title: ConfigurationManager Static Access Must Be Replaced

issues.impact: Correlation tracking approach changes. Built-in ASP.NET Core correlation is more robust. Custom code may not be needed. Estimated effort: 2-4 hours.
issues.description: Using System.Diagnostics.Trace.CorrelationManager for activity tracking should be replaced with ActivitySource.
issues.recommendation: Replace with System.Diagnostics.ActivitySource and Activity. Create ActivitySource at startup. Use Activity.Current for context. ASP.NET Core provides automatic activity correlation. Consider removing custom correlation code and using built-in Activity tracking. Use HttpContext.TraceIdentifier for request correlation.
issues.title: Trace.CorrelationManager Not Recommended in .NET 8

issues.impact: Package can be safely removed. No functionality loss. Estimated effort: 1 hour.
issues.description: Microsoft.CodeDom.Providers.DotNetCompilerPlatform is for runtime compilation in Web Forms, not needed in .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Remove Microsoft.CodeDom.Providers.DotNetCompilerPlatform package. .NET 8 Razor Pages are compiled at build time, not runtime. If runtime compilation needed for development, use Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Razor.RuntimeCompilation package and call AddRazorRuntimeCompilation() in development environment only.
issues.title: Microsoft.CodeDom.Providers Not Needed in .NET 8

issues.impact: Part of overall project file conversion. No isolated work needed. Estimated effort: included in project conversion (issue-12).
issues.description: Project targets .NET Framework 4.7.2, must be changed to net8.0 in SDK-style project.
issues.recommendation: In SDK-style project, use <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework> (singular). Remove TargetFrameworkVersion, TargetFrameworkProfile. Update project SDK to Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web. Remove compatibility shims and legacy properties.
issues.title: TargetFramework Version Must Be Updated to net8.0

issues.impact: Bundling approach changes. File can be deleted after migrating bundle definitions. Estimated effort: included in bundling migration (issue-19).
issues.description: Bundle.config file for System.Web.Optimization is not applicable in .NET 8.
issues.recommendation: Remove Bundle.config file. Migrate bundling configuration to WebOptimizer or build tool configuration. Reference individual CSS/JS files in development, use bundled versions in production with environment Tag Helper: <link rel="stylesheet" href="~/css/site.css" asp-append-version="true" />
issues.title: Bundle.config Not Used in .NET 8

issues.impact: Project properties cleanup. No functional impact on migration. Estimated effort: 1 hour.
issues.description: Project file contains IIS-specific configuration that's not needed for .NET 8 development.
issues.recommendation: Remove IIS-specific properties from project file. .NET 8 uses Kestrel web server by default. For IIS deployment, use out-of-process hosting with web.config generated at publish time. Development uses dotnet run with Kestrel. IIS configuration handled separately via launchSettings.json if needed.
issues.title: IIS Configuration Not Required for .NET 8

issues.impact: Feature detection may need updates or removal. Check if Modernizr is actually needed. Estimated effort: 2-3 hours.
issues.description: Application uses Modernizr 2.8.3 which is quite old. Consider updating or removing if not needed.
issues.recommendation: Update Modernizr to latest version (3.x+) or remove if not needed. Modern browsers support most features that Modernizr was originally needed for. Review actual Modernizr feature detection usage and consider removing if targeting modern browsers only.
issues.title: Modernizr Script May Need Update

issues.impact: Simplified browser support. Remove legacy code. No functional impact on modern browsers. Estimated effort: 1-2 hours.
issues.description: Respond.js is for IE8 support which is no longer necessary. Package can be removed.
issues.recommendation: Remove Respond package and script references. Target modern browsers only (Edge, Chrome, Firefox, Safari). Update browser support policy. Remove IE-specific polyfills and workarounds.
issues.title: Respond.js Not Needed for Modern Browser Support

issues.codeSnippet: Models, Services, and UI all in single project
issues.impact: Complete solution restructuring. Create multiple projects. Move code to appropriate layers. Update references. Estimated effort: 20-30 hours.
issues.description: Current application has business logic mixed with UI layer. Should implement clean architecture with separate projects.
issues.recommendation: Refactor to clean architecture: 1) Domain project with entities and interfaces, 2) Application project with services and DTOs, 3) Infrastructure project with EF Core and repositories, 4) Web project with Razor Pages. Separate concerns and improve testability. Follow upgrade rules architecture guidelines.
issues.title: Clean Architecture Layer Separation Needed

issues.impact: Service layer refactoring. Create repository layer. Update dependency injection. Improve testability. Estimated effort: 12-16 hours.
issues.description: Services directly use DbContext. Should implement repository pattern for better separation and testability.
issues.recommendation: Create repository interfaces in Domain layer (IRepository<T>, ICatalogItemRepository). Implement repositories in Infrastructure layer with DbContext. Inject repositories into services instead of DbContext. Services become orchestration layer without direct database access. Improve unit testing with repository mocks.
issues.title: Repository Pattern Should Be Implemented

issues.impact: Create DTO and ViewModel classes. Add mapping logic. Update all PageModels and views. Configure AutoMapper. Estimated effort: 10-15 hours.
issues.description: Domain entities (CatalogItem) are used directly in views. Should use DTOs/ViewModels for better separation.
issues.recommendation: Create DTO classes in Application layer for data transfer. Create ViewModels in Web layer for UI. Use AutoMapper to map between entities and DTOs. Manually map between DTOs and ViewModels in PageModels. Protects domain model from UI concerns. Allows independent evolution of layers.
issues.title: DTOs Should Be Used Instead of Domain Entities in UI

issues.impact: Add comprehensive test coverage. Create test infrastructure. Write unit and integration tests. Validate migration correctness. Estimated effort: 30-40 hours.
issues.description: Application has no unit tests. Should add test projects as part of migration.
issues.recommendation: Create test projects: 1) UnitTests project for service and business logic testing with xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions. 2) IntegrationTests project for repository and page testing with WebApplicationFactory. Follow upgrade rules testing standards. Aim for 80% code coverage on services. Write tests during migration to validate behavior.
issues.title: No Unit Tests Exist in Current Project

recommendations: 1. Replace Entity Framework 6 with EF Core 8 - This is the foundation for data access. 2. Migrate Global.asax to Program.cs - Required for application startup. 3. Convert Web.config to appsettings.json - Essential configuration migration. 4. Replace log4net with ILogger<T> - Needed throughout application. 5. Convert .csproj to SDK-style targeting net8.0 - Project foundation.

Migrate Web Forms pages to Razor Pages incrementally: Start with simpler pages (About, Contact) to establish patterns. Then migrate CRUD pages (Create, Edit, Delete, Details). Finally migrate complex pages (Default with ListView). Create reusable layout and components first. Test each page migration thoroughly before proceeding.

Implement clean architecture during migration: Create separate projects for Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Web layers. Implement repository pattern for data access. Create DTOs and ViewModels for proper layer separation. Use dependency injection throughout. This investment pays off in maintainability.

Build test infrastructure alongside migration: Create unit test project for service layer testing. Create integration test project for repository and page testing. Write tests as you migrate each component to validate correctness. Aim for 80% code coverage. Use tests to catch migration issues early.

Replace incompatible packages first: 1. EntityFramework 6.2.0 → EF Core 8.0.0 (critical). 2. log4net → Microsoft.Extensions.Logging or Serilog (critical). 3. Autofac.Web → Autofac.Extensions.DependencyInjection or built-in DI (high). 4. All Microsoft.AspNet.* packages → ASP.NET Core equivalents (high). Remove unused packages (Respond.js, old compilers).

Migrate all configuration systematically: Create appsettings.json with sections for ConnectionStrings, AppSettings, Logging. Create appsettings.Development.json for dev-specific config. Implement Options pattern for strongly-typed settings. Replace all ConfigurationManager access with IConfiguration injection. Update documentation for new configuration approach.

Redesign state management: Configure session state in Program.cs with distributed memory cache. Evaluate if session state is truly needed or if stateless design is better. For production, plan for distributed cache (Redis) instead of in-memory. Remove HttpContext.Current usage. Use IHttpContextAccessor for context access in services.

Replace HTTP modules with middleware: Create middleware for custom logic from HTTP modules. Use built-in middleware for common scenarios (logging, authentication, CORS). Configure middleware pipeline in Program.cs. Replace Autofac HTTP modules with constructor injection. Update Application Insights to ASP.NET Core SDK.

Migrate to modern data access patterns: Convert DbContext to EF Core with DbContextOptions. Create separate entity configuration classes implementing IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>. Convert database initialization to EF Core migrations. Add async/await to all data operations. Implement repository pattern for better testability. Add proper error handling and logging.

Review and update security practices: ASP.NET Core has built-in CSRF protection - ensure it's enabled. Review all input validation and use data annotations. Implement proper authentication if needed (ASP.NET Core Identity). Review authorization requirements. Update to HTTPS. Remove deprecated security settings from Web.config. Follow OWASP security guidelines.
